replication.target_description: Direct relationship between performance and satisfaction, considered separately from the pathway through disconfirmation (Shenzhen sample). Regression-based path analysis in §5 (Figure 4 discussed on p. 785); distinct from Table 1 factorial regression.

es.location: p. 785, §5 Results, regression-based path analysis; coefficient metric in adjacent caption
es.quote:
Unstandardized regression coefficients
are shown, with standardized coefficients in parentheses. Hong Kong Model R2 = 0.45; sample size n = 992. Shenzhen Model
R2 = 0.51; sample size n = 1228. *p < 0.10, **p < 0.05, ***p < 0.01 ... There was over a 1 point increase (Hong Kong: 1.121, Shenzhen: 1.243) in satisfaction when the par-
ticipants were exposed to the high-performance photograph.

p.location: p. 785, §5 Results; Figure 4 paths discussed in text, adjacent significance legend
p.quote:
Across the two cities, all of the core relationships were statistically
significant and in the same direction as predicted in the expectation-disconfirmation model and in Van Ryzin's (2013) orig-
inal study (the relationship between expectations and satisfaction for the Shenzhen participants was significant at the
lower threshold of p < 0.1).
